findings.title: Factual/pedagogical error: Charge Nurse writing clinical M&M, and safeguarding misses triggering M&M
findings.body:
In `src/ui/encounter/RotaClosingNote.tsx`, McGrath tells the player to "Read Akin's M&M write-up". In the NHS, a Charge Nurse (Akin) does not write the formal clinical Morbidity and Mortality (M&M) report for a missed aortic dissection; this is a medical governance task typically authored by a consultant or senior registrar. This also contradicts Akin's own handover at position 16, which correctly notes "McGrath wrote the M&M" for the previous patient.

Additionally, in `src/state/consultant.ts` (rotaIndex 13), McGrath says of the Stan and Chloe safeguarding pattern: "Read the M&M when it lands." Safeguarding and psychosocial follow-up failures do not trigger an M&M (which is reserved for significant clinical morbidity/mortality); they trigger a safeguarding review, Datix, or MDT case review.
findings.recommendation:
1. In `RotaClosingNote.tsx`, change "Read Akin's M&M write-up" to "Read my M&M write-up" or "Read Akin's Datix".
2. In `src/state/consultant.ts` (index 13), change "Read the M&M when it lands" to "Read the safeguarding review when it lands" or "Read the incident report".

overall_take: The narrative arc and dual-register voice are exceptionally well-crafted and land the NTS pedagogy beautifully, but there are NHS governance factual errors regarding who writes an M&M and what triggers one that need correcting.
